skill.name: knowledge-work-legal
skill.description: Use when an in-house legal team needs help with contract review, NDA triage, compliance workflows, legal briefs, or precedent research against a configured playbook.
whenToUse: Reviewing a vendor contract clause-by-clause against your organization's negotiation playbook and generating redlines
Rapidly triaging an incoming NDA into approve / counsel-review / escalate buckets
Checking existing agreements, DPAs, and expiration dates for a vendor across connected systems
Preparing a daily legal brief or a research brief on a specific legal question

keyConcepts.explanation: Playbook-based contract analysis that classifies deviations, generates redline language, and flags clauses GREEN / YELLOW / RED with business-impact context.
Screens incoming NDAs against standard criteria and routing rules, categorizing each as standard approval, counsel review, or significant-issue escalation.
Covers privacy regulations like GDPR and CCPA, DPA review, and data subject requests to keep processing workflows compliant.
A risk severity framework with classification levels and escalation criteria for deciding what needs senior or outside counsel review.
A legal.local.md file encodes your standard positions, acceptable ranges, and escalation triggers so review reflects your team's terms and risk tolerance.
vendor-check reports existing NDAs/MSAs/DPAs and key terms for a vendor; meeting-briefing provides meeting prep, context gathering, and action-item tracking.

gotchas: This plugin assists with legal work but does not provide legal advice; AI analysis must be reviewed by a licensed attorney
Default playbook examples reflect U.S. jurisdictions (Delaware, New York, California); customize legal.local.md for EU/UK/other systems before relying on it
Without a configured playbook, contract review has no organization-specific positions to flag deviations against
The plugin degrades gracefully when MCP tools are unavailable, noting gaps and suggesting manual checks rather than guessing
Templated responses include built-in escalation triggers; some inquiry types should not receive a templated reply
